subject: Recap: token economics, budget guardrails, and next steps (FinCap)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Walters <ewalters@fincap.com>, Samantha Cho <scho@fincap.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: token economics, budget guardrails, and next steps (FinCap)

Hi Ethan + Samantha — thanks again for the demo and the candid discussion earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned.

What we heard (pain / goal):
- Primary pain: QA & latency spikes when enabling assistant features in customer flows (fraud reviews and agent assist).
- Budget guardrail: Finance indicated a hard cap in the short term (~$60k/mo) while they validate ROI.
- Success metrics: 1) Keep average end-to-end latency below ~500ms p50, 2) Reduce per-interaction cost to a level that supports 10–15% conversion uplift economics.

Workload profile you shared (from today):
- Monthly token volume: ~3.0M tokens (your export sample attached).
- Avg tokens per session: ~350 (prompt + completion).
- Peak concurrent interactive sessions: small bursty peaks during business hours.

Cost levers we discussed (implications / quick estimates):
- Batching: enabling small request batching for non-interactive reranking and some async flows can lower per-token cost ~20–35% depending on latency tolerance.
- Prefix/KV caching: for repeated prompts (templates & system messages) we expect 10–25% token reduction on average.
- Model quantization / smaller family: moving from a 13B -> 7B quantized variant can reduce unit cost 30–50% with some quality tradeoffs — we can include A/B evals in the pilot.

Immediate asks / next steps (what we’ll deliver):
1) 2-scenario TCO: hosted API pilot (3M tokens/mo) vs. small dedicated capacity (steady baseline + burst). Line-item breakdown (tokens, inference compute, egress) by EOW Aug 20.
2) Pilot proposal: 6-week scope with a 30-day observability window (we’ll include eval sets to monitor quality regressions). Draft attached.
3) Data ask from you: sample token CSV (attached) + any SSO/security questionnaire items procurement needs so we can surface them to our security/compliance team.

Can we tentatively book a 30-min follow-up on Tue Aug 25 10:00 AM PT to review the TCO scenarios and pilot SOW? If procurement prefers a separate call, we’ll schedule that as well.

Attachments: [fincap_token_sample.csv], [redwood-cost-snapshot.pdf]

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the detailed scenarios and a short slide summary.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0121

Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: token economics, budget guardrails, and next steps (FinCap)

Thanks Neha — appreciate the clear write-up. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Confirmed budget cap: finance is targeting ~$60k/month for the first 3 months while we validate conversion impact. That’s a firm ceiling for the pilot contract.
- Procurement timeline: internal procurement aims to complete supplier onboarding by the end of Q3 (Sep 30) if the initial SOW is accepted.
- Quality tolerance: we can accept a modest model-size tradeoff as long as rate of 'nonsensical responses' stays below 1% on sampled evals.

We’ll upload a larger token sample to the Drive link you requested; for now I attached the CSV you requested. Also — procurement asked for a line-item estimate they can review (hosting vs compute vs support) and an example SLI/SLA we would expect for a hosted pilot.

Would Tue Aug 25 10:00 AM PT work for us — please send a calendar invite.

—Ethan
Ethan Walters
Head of Product — FinCap Solutions
ewalters@fincap.com | +1 (212) 555-0890

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: token economics, budget guardrails, and next steps (FinCap)

Neha — quick internal alignment and ops asks before we send the formal TCO: 
- Can you build 2 TCO scenarios: (A) Hosted API pilot at 3M tokens/mo with batching + caching on, (B) Small Dedicated baseline with 2x burstable nodes (we’ll model 99th percentile burst windows). Include monthly amortized cost and per-interaction projected cost.
- Add a separate column for a quantized 7B variant estimate (quality caveat).
- Add a one-paragraph risk note on scaling latency under burst — call out what fallback policy we’d recommend (model fallback -> region fallback -> degrade features).

Marissa — can you include a short checklist of compliance artifacts to attach (SOC2 baseline, data retention options, KMS integration notes) — we’ll need that for procurement.

Also recommend we propose a 6-week pilot with a 4-week measurement window (to capture seasonal variance) and a clear go/no-go criterion tied to per-interaction cost and conversion lift. I’ll join the Aug 25 call — will prepare an ops slide.

-Karthik
